controls.verification: GitHub account MFA must remain enabled for maintainers and token automation must not read personal credentials.
New collaborators receive repository read permission by default; elevated roles require owner action.
The main ruleset blocks direct updates and requires the static-checks-42 status check.
The main ruleset blocks branch deletion.
Every workflow declares explicit read-first permissions and workflow_policy rejects missing or write-all permissions.
Workflow metadata is passed through environment variables or strict tag/version checks; shell input interpolation is tested.
Pull-request jobs have read-only permissions, disable checkout credential persistence, and do not receive publishing secrets.
Release versions come from package.json and tag jobs fail unless the tag equals v<version>.
Official channels are documented with HTTPS; the source policy rejects plaintext transport and URL credentials.
Release artifacts are published through npm/GitHub with checksums and GitHub OIDC build attestations.
CHANGELOG.md is required by the release process and release notes are generated from the tagged commit.
Package manifests, lock files, hashed pip requirements, and Dependabot are present.
Tag workflow attests the tarball and SBOM subjects through GitHub OIDC and uploads a SHA256SUMS manifest.
Sensitive file patterns are ignored and every CI run scans common credential token forms.
README, quickstart, CLI help, and user documentation cover installation and primary functionality.
SUPPORT.md and issue templates provide public defect-reporting instructions.
The dependency and supplier policy documents selection, source, lock, review, update, and removal rules.
CONTRIBUTING documents the build and test commands; release builder has a single documented entry point.
MAINTAINERS.md and CODEOWNERS identify the owner with access to sensitive repository resources.
MAINTAINERS.md describes owner responsibilities and final decision authority.
Public GitHub issues and discussions through pull requests are documented support channels.
CONTRIBUTING and the pull-request template define the contribution process.
CONTRIBUTING defines code style, tests, verification gates, and submission requirements.
The CLA workflow requires a recorded contributor agreement before merge.
Source code is offered under OSI-approved AGPL-3.0-only with documented additional permissions.
The npm tarball includes the same AGPL license and declares it in package metadata and SBOMs.
The source license is present at the repository root.
The release builder includes LICENSE in the npm tarball and validates its presence.
The canonical GitHub repository is public at a stable URL.
GitHub preserves public commit history, authors, and timestamps without automatic history rewriting.
Python, npm, and Rust dependency manifests/locks are tracked, and CI requirements are pinned.
The main ruleset requires static-checks-42 and disallows bypass actors.
NinFenz releases are built from this single canonical repository; the Gitee surface is a mirror, not a second build source.
controls.gap: The requirement applies only when multiple source repositories are compiled into one release.

controls.verification: Scorecard Binary-Artifacts is enabled and generated npm/engine outputs are ignored rather than tracked.
Executable build outputs are generated at build time; tracked image assets are reviewable content assets.
Every pull request runs verify, 32 test shards, and dedicated packaging/release tests.
Supply-chain actors, trust boundaries, release flow, and external interfaces are documented.
CLI, MCP, package, release, and verification interfaces are documented with their trust boundaries.
A release threat model covers dependency confusion, build compromise, artifact substitution, and maintainer-account compromise.
SECURITY.md defines coordinated private disclosure and remediation-before-publication.
SECURITY.md provides the GitHub Security Advisory contact channel.
The GitHub private advisory URL is the only vulnerability-reporting intake.
Published GitHub Security Advisories are the public vulnerability channel and include affected versions and fixes.
